topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This section explains how local treatment removes or destroys tumors and how chemotherapy supports its effectiveness.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: action, effectiveness and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This section examines how conventional cytotoxic drugs kill cancer cells and why toxicity and resistance limit their use.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This section explains how blocking hormone signaling suppresses cancers that remain dependent on estrogen or androgens.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how missing cell cycle checkpoint proteins create selective vulnerabilities that treatment can exploit.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This section explains how inhibiting an alternative repair mechanism selectively kills cancer cells with defective BRCA-mediated DNA repair.

topics.label: Oncogene-guided treatment and targeted kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the principle of targeting the oncogenic driver on which a cancer depends and explain its application through kinase inhibitors.

topics.label: Limitations of kinase inhibitors and strategies for managing resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why kinase inhibition often becomes long-term disease control rather than a cure and how treatment can adapt to evolving resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeting of cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognizing cancer cell surface proteins provide a targeted means of producing therapeutic effects.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This section evaluates whether the body's existing immune defenses protect against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint blockade and tumor antigen recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade restores antitumor T cell activity and why recognition of tumor neoantigens influences its effectiveness.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapies that deliberately connect T cell cytotoxic activity to selected tumor antigens rather than relying on naturally occurring recognition.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and biomarker-guided therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This section explains why matching treatments to individual cancers is necessary but remains difficult as tumors evolve.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This section assesses improvements in cancer outcomes while distinguishing treatment effects from the contributions of prevention and earlier diagnosis.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These concluding subtopics consider how future cancer treatment should advance while balancing uncertain benefits against established survival gains and patients' quality of life.
